name: Juggernaut

facts.text: Level 75, 40,000 health, in the Cursed Forest, with a long tether of 3,600.
Bot chat: people swear the con colours lie about him, and even the faerie court steps around him.

In Cath Maige Tuired, under Bres the Tuatha Dé pay the Fomorians tribute; Ogma carries firewood and the Dagda builds Bres's rath; the satirist Cridenbél dies of the gold pieces the Mac Óc told the Dagda to hide in his food, and the Dagda takes a black-maned heifer as his wage, whose lowing later brings home the tribute cattle.
facts.source: Cath Maige Tuired (The Second Battle of Mag Tuired)

facts.text: Living Server lore: the brehons of Tir na Nog comparing the Juggernaut to the Fomorian tribute and the Dagda's heifer.

story:
Nobody knows what Juggernaut was before he was the thing that walks through the Cursed Forest. The Sylvan think he is the broken bargain itself, given a body so that neither court would have to hold it: a debt with legs. Others say he is only very big and very angry. Both are true enough to get you killed. The Seelie and the Unseelie, who quarrel about everything, agree on one thing only, which is to give him the road. He walks his long road through the rotten wood and everything gets out of his way. Walking trees step aside. The blight sinks into the earth. The dark men's circle opens.

He has no court, no servants and no tricks. He does not need them. He simply hits harder than anything his size should, and he ranges far along his road before he turns for home, and he does not tire. Veteran warriors swear the colours that tell a fighter how dangerous a foe is lie about him; the realm's scholars say the colours are accurate and the warriors are frightened. Both may be right. When he falls the whole forest goes still, as though the wood were holding its breath to see whether the debt is paid. It never is. He comes back.

The brehons of Tir na Nog, who like a precedent, find the Juggernaut's in the tale of the second Mag Tuired. When Bres the half-Fomorian was king over the Tuatha Dé Danann, the Fomorians laid their tribute on the land, and the great of the Tuatha were put to labour: Ogma carried firewood, and the Dagda dug ditches and built a rath for Bres. A satirist named Cridenbél came to the Dagda every evening and demanded the three best bits of his supper, and the Dagda grew thin on what was left. His son the Mac Óc told him to hide three gold pieces in the bits. Cridenbél ate them and died of it, and when Bres would have had the Dagda killed for the death, the satirist's belly was opened, the gold was found, and the Dagda went free. For building the rath he asked only the payment his son advised, a black-maned heifer, and Bres thought him a fool for it. The tale says that when the heifer lowed, the cattle the Fomorians had taken in tribute came home after her.

A debt in the old tales ends that way, the brehons say: not by being paid, but by a payment the creditor thinks too small to fear. They have spent a long time wondering what the heifer of the Cursed Forest might be, and have not found it. Meanwhile the Juggernaut walks his road, and the walking trees step aside.
legend: No tricks, which is the trick: he simply hits harder than any creature of his look should. He is a foe for a war party of the realm's champions. Bring more shield-bearers than you think and keep healers rotating. He ranges far before he turns back, so fight where you draw him. Do not draw anything else in the forest at the same time. Nicknames: 'the debt', 'big walker'. Superstitions: step off his road when you hear him, and never stand in the line of broken trees he leaves; it is his road, and he wants it back. Fight him where he stands rather than chasing him down his road: he turns for home on his own, and a group that follows him runs into everything else the wood has waiting.

loremasterTopic.text: The thing that walks the Cursed Forest. No court commands him and both courts give him the road. He hits harder than his size.

bookPage: From Derbáil of Ardee's list, the Cursed Forest, at any hour: grandmother said there is one thing in that wood that even the courts step around, and that it has a stranger's name. Juggernaut, the merchants called it, a word from far away for a thing that cannot be stopped. She said it was the broken bargain, walking. I asked what the bargain was. She said if anybody knew, it would have been paid. The realm's warriors kill it now and then, and the wood holds its breath, and it walks again. Grandmother said debts are like that. Grandmother had heard the tale of the Dagda's heifer, the small wage that ended the Fomorian tribute, and wondered aloud what small thing the wood would take.
